output:
To: posts/new
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Correction: the GST formula in my takings template was wrong (v1.0 to v1.2)

The GST column in my free takings and GST template overstated GST for anyone who keys in GST-inclusive takings. The error was mine. A fixed version, v1.3, has been up since 8 November. Here is what went wrong, who is affected and what to do about it.

**What was wrong**

Column F worked out GST as inclusive takings x 9%. When takings already include GST, the correct calculation is 9/109 of those takings.

Ravi Subramaniam's example shows the gap. His takings on 3 November were $1,090, GST inclusive. The template gave GST of $98.10. The correct figure is $90, so the template was $8.10 too high on that one day. The old result is always 1.09 times the correct GST, which means it overstated GST by 9%.

Thank you to Ravi and to Shu Fen of Numbers For Hawkers for catching this and saying so openly.

**Who is affected**

- Versions v1.0 (12 Aug), v1.1 (2 Sep) and v1.2 (1 Oct). The template has been downloaded 412 times since 12 August. If you downloaded it before 8 November, assume you have an affected version.
- Only people who enter GST-inclusive takings, which is most hawkers. If the amounts you keyed in already excluded GST, 9% was the right rate and your figures were fine.
- Only the GST figure was wrong. The quarterly Box 1 sales total is calculated separately and was correct. Box 6 is the one that was overstated.

**How I missed it**

When I tested v1.0, I used sample figures that were already ex-GST. On those, x 9% is correct, so the check passed. I never ran it against inclusive takings, which is how most of you actually record them. No excuses. That was a gap in my testing.

**Overpaid, not underpaid**

Because the error overstates GST, nobody should have underpaid IRAS because of it. Some of you may have overpaid. Melvin, you are right to be upset. People used this template partly because I am an accountant, and that is exactly why I should have tested it properly.

**What to do now**

1. Download v1.3 from the template post. The changelog is alongside.
2. Check cell H2 and set it to match the amounts you enter. Choose "prices exclude GST" only for entries that exclude GST. For receipts that include the GST you collected, use the inclusive setting, even if your menu prices are shown without GST.
3. Re-check your figures. Add up your inclusive takings for the quarter and multiply by 9/109. Compare the result with the GST on your quarterly tab. For Ravi's $1,090 day, that gives $90.
4. If you have not filed yet, use the v1.3 figures for your return.
5. If you have already filed, such as Jul to Sep, do not simply change your records and hope for the best. IRAS has its own rules on whether an error is corrected in a later F5 or needs a GST F7. I am not going to paraphrase those rules, because you should get them from the source. Read the IRAS page on correcting errors in GST returns, then speak to your filer or tax agent about which route applies to you.

I earlier asked people to hold off changing their records until I had confirmed the cause. That is now done, so you can go ahead with the steps above.

If anything about the template itself is unclear, leave a comment and I will answer it. For your own filing position, though, IRAS and your filer are the right people to ask.
